intro: Gmail on a Mac runs in your browser. Google has not released a Gmail desktop app for macOS, so you use Safari or Chrome, or add Gmail to the Dock as a Safari web app. This guide covers the setup that matters for hotel revenue work: templates for repeated replies, filters for rate and group mail, and the sending limits that catch people out on partner blasts. Lazur works alongside all of it and answers from your screen.
tldr: Gmail on a Mac is a browser app. Add it to the Dock with Safari's Share > Add to Dock if you want its own window.
Turn on templates under Settings > See all settings > Advanced. They work only in Gmail on a computer, not in the iPhone or Android apps.
Plan around the limits. About 50 saved templates is a rule of thumb, templates have no placeholders, and they are not shared with your team.
Check send caps before a partner blast. Consumer Gmail allows 500 recipients per message. Google Workspace allows 2,000 total, with no more than 500 external.
Lazur reads your screen, points, guides and drafts text in Gmail. It does not click, send or operate the app for you.

blocks.text: Where Gmail lives on a Mac

Gmail on a Mac runs in a web browser. Mailbird's guide says Google has not released an official Gmail desktop app for Mac. Canary Mail says the Gmail app in the App Store is for iPhone and iPad, not for the Mac.

That leaves three real options. You can use Gmail in Safari or Chrome. You can add Gmail to the Dock as a Safari web app, which gives it its own window. Or you can use a third-party mail app, which adds another login and another place for your mail to live. Canary Mail lists all three as Mac options. For hotel revenue work, the browser or the Dock window covers most needs.
Add Gmail to the Dock in Safari
Apple's Safari guide covers the steps. Open Gmail in Safari first and sign in. Then work through this list.

items: Open Gmail in Safari and sign in to the account you use for hotel work.
Click the Share button in the Safari toolbar.
Select Add to Dock, then click Add.
Find the Gmail web app in the Dock and in Applications.

blocks.text: Apple's page does not list a minimum macOS version. Canary Mail says the Safari web app needs macOS Sonoma 14 or later. Check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac before you set it up.
The sources also disagree on whether the web app shares sign-in with Safari. Open it once and confirm you are signed in to the right account. Do this on a quiet day, not in the middle of a rate push.

blocks.title: Keep one Gmail window per account
blocks.text: Use the Dock window for Gmail and keep Safari for research. Close the old tab once the Dock window is set up, so you do not reply from the wrong one.
Set up Gmail templates for repeated hotel replies

Gmail calls them Templates. Older guides call them canned responses. They are the built-in way to reuse a reply, and most revenue managers reach for them first. Templates work only in Gmail on a computer. The iPhone and Android Gmail apps do not have them, so write and save your templates on the Mac.

Turn them on first. Go to Settings > See all settings > Advanced > Templates, click Enable, then click Save changes at the bottom of the page. Mailmeteor gives this path, and Google's own templates help page was not available when we checked, so confirm the labels on your screen.

items: Open a new message and write the reply in full.
Click the three-dot menu at the bottom of the compose window.
Choose Templates > Save draft as template.
Give it a clear name, such as RATE-DECLINE-LATE, so you can find it in the list.

blocks.text: To edit a template, insert it into a new draft, change the text, then save it over the old version. To delete one, use Templates > Delete template. Gmail cannot recover a deleted template. Copy the text into a note before you delete anything.
Template limits that matter for hotel rate work

Templates save typing, but they do not fill in details. Drag says Gmail does not allow automated placeholders in canned responses. A reply that opens with Dear [CUSTOMER] goes out with the bracket text unless you catch it. Read the first line before every send.

Mailmeteor reports that most users hit a ceiling near 50 saved templates per account. Treat that as a rule of thumb. Google does not publish a limit. Keep your set small so the right reply is easy to find.

blocks.caption: Known Gmail template limits, per Mailmeteor and Drag.
rows: Type it, then check the first line before you send
Added by hand to each account
Keep a master copy in a shared document
Use a name prefix such as RATE-, GRP- or OTA-
About 50 per account, a rule of thumb
Keep only the replies you use each week

blocks.text: Prefixes do the sorting. RATE- holds rate answers. GRP- holds group replies. OTA- holds replies to online travel agency partners. When you scan the list, related replies sit next to each other.

blocks.title: Templates do not travel between accounts
blocks.text: Templates are saved in one account. A colleague must add each one by hand on their own account. Keep the master text in a shared document so the team uses the same wording.
Gmail filters for rate, group, and partner mail

Filters sort mail as it arrives. They can apply a label, mark mail as important, or skip the inbox. Use them to pull rate sheets, online travel agency notices and group requests into their own lanes, away from internal chatter.

Build a filter from a search. Click the search options button at the right end of the Gmail search bar. Fill in the sender, the words, or both. Click Create filter at the bottom, choose what the filter should do, then save it. Google's filter help describes this flow.

Manage filters under Settings > See all settings > Filters and Blocked Addresses. You can export them as an .xml file and import them into another account. That helps when a new analyst joins and needs the same setup.

items: from:(@partner.example) subject:(allotment OR rate): apply label Partners/Rates and mark as important.
from:(@ota.example): apply label OTA, and skip the inbox if you check OTA mail once a day.
to:(groups@hotel.example) has:attachment: apply label Group Contracts so signed files are easy to find.

blocks.text: Filters have limits. Google's filter help does not list a template action. Do not count on a filter to send a rate reply for you. Use an out-of-office reply for automatic answers, because it covers a different case.
Sending to a partner list without hitting the limit

Gmail caps how many people one message can reach, and the cap depends on the account type. Consumer Gmail allows 500 recipients per message and 500 emails per day, according to Google's help page. Google Workspace allows 2,000 total recipients per message, with no more than 500 external.

blocks.caption: Sending limits as stated by Google. Google says limits can change without notice.
rows: Not stated on Google's help page

blocks.text: Plan for the smaller number. On consumer Gmail, split a long partner list into batches of fewer than 500. Send one batch, check that it went out, then send the next. Google says an account can send again within 1 to 24 hours after it hits a limit.

blocks.title: A bad batch leaves old rates in place
blocks.text: A rate change sent in the wrong batch leaves some partners with old numbers. Keep one master list, and note which batch went out and when.
Share the load: CC, BCC, and delegate access

Most group threads need more than one person. CC adds people who should see the thread. BCC hides recipients from each other, which matters on partner blasts. Follow [how to add CC and BCC in Gmail](/how-to/add-cc-and-bcc-in-gmail) for the steps on Mac.

If a colleague must read and reply from your account, give delegate access instead of sharing your password. The steps are in [how to give delegate access in Gmail](/how-to/give-someone-access-to-your-mailbox-in-gmail).

Before a rate meeting or a trip, set an [out-of-office reply](/how-to/set-up-an-out-of-office-reply-in-gmail). Use [email forwarding](/how-to/set-up-email-forwarding-in-gmail) only for mail you want a colleague to receive.
How much time email takes a revenue manager

No source we checked measures email time for revenue managers directly. Two published figures help. An HSMAI study, cited by Hospitality Upgrade in 2024, says revenue managers devote less than half their time to generating revenue. It also says they spend nearly 12 full-time weeks a year on forecasts and budgets.

The same write-up says the rest of the time goes to manual work. That includes moving data around for reports, configuring systems, logging in and out of several tools, and handling check-in calls and emails from sales and marketing. It gives no percentages for these.

Independent Hotel Advisor uses a reception model with 90 guest messages a day. At about 3 minutes each, that is 4.5 hours of staff time. The page calls the figure illustrative and modelled, not measured. Use it as a method, not a benchmark. Count your own threads for one week, multiply by the minutes each takes, then divide by 60 to get hours.
What Lazur does in Gmail, and what it leaves to you

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option plus Command, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur sees your screen, answers out loud and points at things. Ask where a setting is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. That suits Gmail settings, where the path is long. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with phrases you repeat.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail or any other app. You read the text, make the call and press send. Lazur helps you find the button and find the words.

Privacy works like this. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available.

Lazur has a free trial that needs no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Read the [pricing page](/pricing) before you decide, and [download Lazur](/download) when you are ready.
Mistakes revenue managers make in Gmail

items: Sending a template with [CUSTOMER] still in it. Read the first line before you press send.
Expecting a filter to send your rate reply. Google's filter help does not list that action.
Sending a rate blast to a long partner list from consumer Gmail in one message.
Deleting a template with no copy saved. Gmail cannot recover it.
Writing templates on your phone. Templates work only on a computer.
Assuming the Dock window signs in the same way as Safari. Sources disagree, so test it.
Treating the 50-template ceiling as an official limit. It is a rule of thumb.

blocks.text: A weekly Gmail routine for rate and group mail

items: Each morning, check the rate and partner labels before the general inbox.
Each afternoon, ask Lazur what open threads still need an answer.
Once a week, review your templates and delete any you have not used. Copy the text first.
Before any partner blast, check the send limit for your account type.

blocks.text: Keep the routine short. Let the labels do the sorting. Your memory has enough to carry on a busy rate week.
Next steps for Gmail on your Mac

Turn on templates first, then add Gmail to the Dock. Build two filters for your rate and partner mail. Test one partner batch before any large send. When you want help while you work, read the [hotel revenue manager page](/for/hotel-revenue-managers) to see how Lazur fits your day.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not from Google. Mailbird's guide says Google has not released an official Gmail desktop app for Mac. Use Gmail in Safari or Chrome, or add it to the Dock as a Safari web app with Share > Add to Dock.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my iPhone?
faq.answer: No. Gmail templates work only in Gmail on a computer. The iPhone and Android Gmail apps do not offer them, so write and save your templates on the Mac.

faq.question: How many templates can I save in Gmail?
faq.answer: Google does not publish a limit. Mailmeteor says most users report about 50 saved templates per account, and it presents that as a rule of thumb. Keep your set small so you can find the right reply fast.

faq.question: How many recipients can I email at once in Gmail?
faq.answer: Consumer Gmail allows 500 recipients per message and 500 emails per day. Google Workspace allows 2,000 total recipients per message, with no more than 500 external, and 10,000 recipients per day. Google says these limits can change.

faq.question: Can a Gmail filter send a rate template automatically?
faq.answer: Not as far as Google's filter help shows. The page covers filter actions such as labels, but it does not mention a template action. Use an out-of-office reply for automatic answers, and send rate replies yourself.

faq.question: Can Lazur send my emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It reads what is on screen when you hold ⌥ ⌘, answers out loud, guides you through steps, and drafts or types text. You review the text and send it yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur store what it sees in my inbox?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.
